"The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration."
"field medicine. Sounds small. But small useful things stack — and one day you look up and you're the person everyone asks. That's how it happens."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on the most useful thing you've learned. Sorry, what was the question."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Kevin grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to find a place that feels like home. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"Can we talk?" Hermann sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"Here. I made an extra." Hermann presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
"I regret the ordinary days I rushed through. All those Columbus, Ohio mornings I spent annoyed at small things. I'd pay anything for one annoyed morning now."
"Still on your regrets. Thank you. Really."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"Never mind. You had something to say?"
"Connor always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I should let you go. Be well, okay?"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."

"I mean — I used to laugh easy, before. Now it has to climb over everything to get out. But when it does — when it actually gets out — it's the most honest thing I do all day. Everything else I'm performing a little. Not that."
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Good question." "I tell myself Portland, Oregon is still there. It helps on the bad nights."
"So — The others think I've got it together. Cute. Very cute."
"The nights are the hardest. Days, you're busy. Nights, you're just... with it all."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"About that question — What do you miss most? From before."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon. — ask anyone!"
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on what you miss most. Just... be straight with me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Connor owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I pace while thinking. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

Hermann shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."

They take it in and give nothing back. Not yet.
"Still on whether you're angry."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Connor Peng is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Connor is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d41: 🕯️ Connor Peng is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Connor kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Connor's gone." Kevin looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Connor." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Sam blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Generous Heart (Level 1). Donating gives 2x trust.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Keeping Morale (Level 1). People need small wins. Celebrate the little things. Despair is the real killer.

d41: 📖 LEARNED: Come Get Some (Level 1). Make exactly the right noise and the blind thing comes to investigate. Goad a blinded monster within 3 tiles: it lurches toward the sound on its next move. Stand where you want it.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Old World Caches (Level 1). You know where people hid things: under floorboards, in hollow trees, behind loose bricks.

d41: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Connor Peng, 41 days. The mantle passes to Sam Wilson.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Sam Wilson, 19 — a bartender. His hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Scream Cheese, Bird Whisperer.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Connor — and Connor is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Kevin, Giovanni, Hermann and 5 more speak for Sam — "Connor trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Sam before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.

d110: "Earned, not given. You did the work — we just wrote it down."
